# dyadMLM: Tools for Dyadic Multilevel Models <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="139" alt="dyadMLM package logo" />

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/Pascal-Kueng/dyadMLM/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Pascal-Kueng/dyadMLM/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/Pascal-Kueng/dyadMLM/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/Pascal-Kueng/dyadMLM)
[![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/dyadMLM)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=dyadMLM)
[![CRAN downloads](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/grand-total/dyadMLM)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=dyadMLM)
[![DOI](https://img.shields.io/badge/DOI-10.5281%2Fzenodo.21481720-blue.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21481720)
<!-- badges: end -->

Dyadic data come from pairs of people, such as couples, parent–child pairs, or
patients and their caregivers. Responses from the two partners are usually
related, and multilevel models can account for this.

`dyadMLM` provides tools for dyadic multilevel modeling with linear and
generalized linear mixed-effects models.

It provides functions for data preparation for various types of
dyadic models and post-estimation tools for interpretation and checking of model
assumptions.

If you use `dyadMLM`, please cite it as:

`r citation_text`

To include the version you used, see [Citation](#citation).

## Where to start

| Vignette | Focus |
|---|---|
| [Getting Started](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/articles/getting-started.html) | Data structure, validation, dyad compositions, generated columns, and basic preparation |
| [Actor-Partner Interdependence Model](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/articles/apim.html) | Cross-sectional and longitudinal APIMs, distinguishability checks, covariance recovery, random slopes, and AR(1) |
| [Dyad-Individual Model](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/articles/dim.html) | DIM predictor construction, longitudinal models, and an interactive demonstration of equivalence to the exchangeable APIM |
| [Dyadic Score Model](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/articles/dsm.html) | DSM predictor-score and contrast construction, longitudinal models, and the relationship to the distinguishable APIM |

Each model vignette has a section on intensive longitudinal data
([APIM](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/articles/apim.html#intensive-longitudinal-apims),
[DIM](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/articles/dim.html#intensive-longitudinal-dim),
[DSM](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/articles/dsm.html#intensive-longitudinal-dsm)),
and Getting Started covers
[multiple dyad compositions](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/articles/getting-started.html#working-with-multiple-dyad-compositions).
The model-fitting examples use **glmmTMB**.

For theoretical foundations and a practical walkthrough of dyadic data analysis,
from data preparation and model fitting to interpretation and diagnostics using
`dyadMLM` with `glmmTMB`, see the
[Dyadic Data Analysis Workshop](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/workshop/).
For Bayesian APIM and DIM workflows using `dyadMLM` and `brms`, refer to
[Distinguishable and Exchangeable Dyads: Bayesian Multilevel Modelling](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/05DyadicDataAnalysis/)
([source](https://github.com/Pascal-Kueng/05DyadicDataAnalysis),
[DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17400655)).

For an overview of the available functions, see the
[function reference](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/reference/index.html).

## Installation

Install the stable release from CRAN:

```{r eval = FALSE}
install.packages("dyadMLM")
```

To try the latest changes and help test upcoming features, install the
development version:

```{r eval = FALSE}
install.packages(
  "dyadMLM",
  repos = c(
    "https://pascal-kueng.r-universe.dev",
    "https://cloud.r-project.org"
  )
)
```

## Quick example

Using the bundled simulated data, we select female–male dyads and, for
illustration, fit an APIM that treats partners as exchangeable. We then check
whether it reproduces gender-specific variation and partner dependence.

This example requires the development version of **dyadMLM**. It also uses
**glmmTMB**.

```{r cross-sectional-prep}
library(dyadMLM)

prepared_data <- prepare_dyad_data(
  dyads_cross,
  dyad = coupleID,
  member = personID,
  role = gender,
  predictors = provided_support,
  model_types = "apim",
  keep_compositions = "female-male",
  add_apim_gmc_predictors = TRUE,
  include_arbitrary_member_contrast = TRUE,
  seed = 123
)
```

This creates grand-mean-centred actor and partner predictors and a member
contrast for the exchangeable model. Inspect the prepared data with `print()`:

```{r prepared-data-preview}
print(prepared_data, n = 4)
```

Fit the exchangeable APIM:

```{r cross-sectional-model}
model <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
  closeness ~
    # Pooled intercept
    1 +

    # Pooled actor and partner effects
    .provided_support_gmc_actor +
    .provided_support_gmc_partner +

    # Mean/half-difference parametrization:
    # common member variance and positive or negative partner correlation
    us(1 | coupleID) +
    us(0 + .member_contrast_arbitrary | coupleID),

  dispformula = ~ 0, # Fix the additional Gaussian residual variance near zero
  family = gaussian(),
  data = prepared_data
)
```

Next, check whether the model reproduces the data.

<details>
<summary>Complete model-checking workflow (click to expand): partner-dependence, residual, and outcome checks for two APIMs, and a model comparison</summary>

Simulate responses and check partner dependence, using gender to distinguish
partners:

```{r cross-sectional-check, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6.5, fig.alt = "Six predictive-check histograms. Gender-specific SDs and partner correlation are in the top row; dyad-average and half-difference summaries are in the bottom row. Red lines mark observed values and dashed lines mark the middle 95 percent of simulations."}
simulations <- simulate_dyad_responses(model, seed = 123)

check_partner_dependence(
  simulations,
  dyad = coupleID,
  role = gender,
  # Supply the fitting data because gender is not in the model formula.
  data = prepared_data
)
```

Here, simulations produce weaker partner correlations and larger SDs of partner
half-differences than observed (red lines), suggesting **misfit**.

It can be worthwhile to check plausible role distinctions even when fitting an
exchangeable model, since a pooled check can hide differences between roles.
Check the residuals and outcomes by gender too, reusing the same `simulations`:

```{r exchangeable-residuals, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8, fig.alt = c("Residual checks for women and men under the exchangeable APIM: uniform QQ plots with blue envelopes in the top row and PIT quartiles across predicted outcomes in the bottom row. Women's red curves rise above the envelopes and men's fall below.", "Mean PIT distance histograms for women and men under the exchangeable APIM. Both red lines lie within the dashed limits.")}
check_dyad_residuals(
  simulations,
  dyad = coupleID,
  role = gender,
  data = prepared_data
)
```

Women's QQ curve and PIT quartiles rise above their envelopes and men's fall
below, so women's observed closeness is higher than simulated and men's is
lower. Both mean PIT distances lie within their limits.

```{r exchangeable-outcomes, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 12, fig.alt = "Outcome checks for women and men under the exchangeable APIM: outcome ECDFs in the top row, then histograms of the response SD and the largest absolute deviation. Women's observed ECDF lies right of the simulated curves and men's left. The red lines in the histograms lie within the dashed limits."}
check_dyad_outcomes(
  simulations,
  dyad = coupleID,
  role = gender,
  data = prepared_data
)
```

The outcome ECDFs show the same shift, while response SDs and largest deviations
stay within their limits.

Fit the distinguishable APIM, which lets intercepts, actor and partner effects,
and residual variances differ by gender:

```{r distinguishable-model}
model_distinguishable <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
  closeness ~
    # Gender-specific intercepts
    0 + .is_female + .is_male +

    # Gender-specific actor and partner effects
    .is_female:.provided_support_gmc_actor +
    .is_male:.provided_support_gmc_actor +
    .is_female:.provided_support_gmc_partner +
    .is_male:.provided_support_gmc_partner +

    # Gender-specific residual variances and their covariance
    us(0 + .is_female + .is_male | coupleID),

  dispformula = ~ 0,
  family = gaussian(),
  data = prepared_data
)
```

Run the same checks on simulations from this model:

```{r distinguishable-dependence, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6.5, fig.alt = "Six predictive-check histograms for the distinguishable APIM, laid out as in the first figure. All red lines lie within the dashed limits."}
simulations_distinguishable <- simulate_dyad_responses(
  model_distinguishable, seed = 123
)

check_partner_dependence(
  simulations_distinguishable,
  dyad = coupleID,
  role = gender,
  data = prepared_data
)
```

All red lines now lie within their dashed limits.

```{r distinguishable-residuals, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8, fig.alt = c("Residual checks for women and men under the distinguishable APIM, laid out as for the exchangeable APIM. All red curves stay within the blue envelopes.", "Mean PIT distance histograms for women and men under the distinguishable APIM. Both red lines lie within the dashed limits.")}
check_dyad_residuals(
  simulations_distinguishable,
  dyad = coupleID,
  role = gender,
  data = prepared_data
)
```

The QQ curves and PIT quartiles stay within their envelopes. The mean PIT
distances lie within their limits.

```{r distinguishable-outcomes, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 12, fig.alt = "Outcome checks for women and men under the distinguishable APIM, laid out as for the exchangeable APIM. The observed ECDFs run among the simulated curves and all red lines lie within the dashed limits."}
check_dyad_outcomes(
  simulations_distinguishable,
  dyad = coupleID,
  role = gender,
  data = prepared_data
)
```

The outcome ECDFs run among the simulated curves, and response SDs and largest
deviations stay within their limits.

These checks alone do not establish whether fixed effects should be pooled.
Compare the two nested models with a likelihood-ratio test:

```{r compare-models}
compare_nested_models(model, model_distinguishable)
```

The test supports the distinguishable APIM (p < 0.001).

The [APIM vignette](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/articles/apim.html)
explains each step.

</details>

## Data preparation and validation

[`prepare_dyad_data()`](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/reference/prepare_dyad_data.html)
validates dyadic data and creates model-ready columns for:

- ✅ **Actor-Partner Interdependence Model (APIM):** distinguishable and exchangeable dyads.
- ✅ **Dyad-Individual Model (DIM):** exchangeable dyads.
- ✅ **Dyadic Score Model (DSM):** distinguishable dyads.

It supports cross-sectional and intensive longitudinal dyadic data (e.g., daily
diary data). The package also supports datasets containing multiple dyad compositions.

Preparation options include selecting and pooling compositions, treating selected
compositions as exchangeable, centering predictors, and creating within-/between-person
components and lagged predictors.

Prepared data can be used with **glmmTMB**, **brms**, and other multilevel modeling
packages that support the required model structure. See the
[Getting Started vignette](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/articles/getting-started.html)
for data requirements and examples.

## Post-estimation tools

| Tool | glmmTMB | brms |
|---|---|---|
| [Compare nested models](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/reference/compare_nested_models.html) | ✅ Supported | Not implemented · [Contribute](https://github.com/Pascal-Kueng/dyadMLM/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) |
| [Recover exchangeable member variances and partner covariances](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/reference/recover_exchangeable_covariance.html) | ✅ Point estimates | ✅ Posterior summaries and draws |
| [Check partner dependence — cross-sectional](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/reference/check_partner_dependence.html) | ✅ Experimental | Not implemented · [Contribute](https://github.com/Pascal-Kueng/dyadMLM/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) |
| [Check residuals](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/reference/check_dyad_residuals.html) | ✅ Experimental | Not implemented · [Contribute](https://github.com/Pascal-Kueng/dyadMLM/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) |
| [Check outcomes](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/reference/check_dyad_outcomes.html) | ✅ Experimental | Not implemented · [Contribute](https://github.com/Pascal-Kueng/dyadMLM/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) |

Predictive checks compare the *observed* data with data simulated from the
fitted model: outcome and residual distributions, variability, and partner
dependence. See
[`simulate_dyad_responses()`](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/reference/simulate_dyad_responses.html)
for supported models. Simulation studies
show how often the partner check detects
[omitted partner dependence](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/articles/partner-dependence-simulation.html)
and [incorrect covariance pooling](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/articles/covariance-pooling.html),
and how often the residual and outcome checks
[flag correct and mismatched models](https://pascal-kueng.github.io/dyadMLM/articles/distribution-checks.html).

## Questions and contributing

Questions about using `dyadMLM`, specifying models, or interpreting output are
welcome in [Q&A Discussions](https://github.com/Pascal-Kueng/dyadMLM/discussions/categories/q-a).

Feature or method ideas can be proposed in
[Ideas](https://github.com/Pascal-Kueng/dyadMLM/discussions/categories/ideas).

Please report any bugs you find or any concrete improvement suggestions
through [Issues](https://github.com/Pascal-Kueng/dyadMLM/issues/new/choose).

Documentation, examples, tests, reviews, and code contributions are all
welcome. See the
[contribution guide](https://github.com/Pascal-Kueng/dyadMLM/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
